The same weights, doing the job they were trained for
Every other page traces a training step. This one shows the same weights doing the job they were trained for, and the differences are worth seeing line by line: no gradients, no
, no correct previous token, and a sequence that grows underneath the mask.

text.tspan: A decorator on the whole method, and the first of two switches that separate using the model from training it. With gradients off,
PyTorch stops recording the operations — no intermediate tensor is kept alive for a backward pass that will never happen,
which saves a lot of memory and time. Forget it and generation still produces the right tokens, but it quietly builds up a record
of every decoding step and holds on to it.

ones before it — and it is also where the model’s mistakes become permanent: whatever was chosen at this step is
part of what every later step reads, right or wrong. Training never had to deal with that, because teacher forcing
always supplied the correct token instead — the gap described in Section C of

The one picture the notebook produces, and what it leaves out

This is the one picture the notebook draws, and it is easy to read too much into. It shows the attention of the FINAL step, from the LAST decoder layer, averaged over four heads that may disagree completely — three separate simplifications before you see a number.
Why the untrained heatmap looks so even
These values are real — the averaged cross-attention of the last decoder layer of this freshly initialised model — which is why they are fairly even: a perfectly even row would give
. An untrained decoder spreads its attention over every source word it is allowed to see, and sequence A’s

C · What the missing key/value cache costs
the same positions, decoded again and again
The gap between a teaching implementation and a production one
This is the one place where the notebook differs from a production implementation in a way that matters for speed rather than correctness, and it is invisible unless you count it.

tspan.style: font-family:'DejaVu Sans Mono', Menlo, Consolas, 'Courier New', monospace;font-size:10.3px;font-weight:600;fill:var(--accent)

text.tspan: Three tokens cost six position-decodes instead of three, because every step re-runs the decoder over the whole prefix. The pattern is
one half a million. Production implementations avoid this with a key/value cache — the

for positions already decoded never change, so they are stored and only the new position is computed. Nothing about the maths changes; the notebook simply leaves it out, and for a three-token output that is the right call.
